notes: Envelope is 10 kW continuous, fed by dedicated 240 V circuits — one 60 A circuit safely delivers 11.5 kW continuous (NEC 80% rule), the same class as a big EV charger. Never spread this load across ordinary 120 V wall outlets.
5 kW solar + battery covers roughly half the worst case; the battery smooths inference bursts and the grid takes the rest.
GPUs run power-limited (nvidia-smi -pl): 3090 at 250 W loses ~4% throughput for ~30% less power.
PSUs run on 240 V — 2-3% better efficiency than 120 V and half the current per conductor.
If a phase needs more than the envelope, the machine moves to an industrial location — that is a planned exit, not a failure.
thermalNotes: Open-air frames, no cases: ambient extraction is the owner's home turf.
Used 3090s get fresh thermal pads on VRAM before entering service.
Exhaust heat is a feature in winter, a ducting problem in summer — duct design owned outside this app.

thermalDesign.title: Heat budget = power budget
thermalDesign.body: Every watt in is a watt of heat out. The full 12-GPU plan at ~4.3 kW is ~14,600 BTU/hr — more heat than a large window AC can remove. At the 10 kW envelope ceiling it is ~34,000 BTU/hr, close to a 3-ton central AC. Extraction is designed for worst case, not average.

thermalDesign.title: Open-air frames
thermalDesign.body: No closed cases anywhere. Open mining-style frames drop GPU hotspot temps 10-15°C versus chassis-bound cards, cost ~$80, and make every component serviceable in seconds.

thermalDesign.title: Power-limited silicon
thermalDesign.body: 3090s capped at 250 W shed ~30% of their heat for ~4% throughput loss — the single highest-leverage thermal decision in the build. GDDR6X junction temperature is the binding constraint, not core temp.

thermalDesign.title: Repad used cards
thermalDesign.body: Mining-era 3090s arrive with cooked VRAM thermal pads and will throttle above 100°C junction. Every used card gets fresh pads on VRAM and VRMs before entering service.

thermalDesign.title: Seasonal ducting
thermalDesign.body: Winter: exhaust ducts into living space — 4 kW of free heating credits the power budget. Summer: insulated duct straight outdoors with a booster fan; intake pulls from the coolest side of the building.

thermalDesign.title: Instrumented, not hoped
thermalDesign.body: nvidia-smi GPU/junction temps and IPMI board sensors stream to mission control. Thermal alarms pause the job queue before hardware ever sees a critical temp.
